summary:
FMLink promotes an episode of the Facility Voices Podcast, produced by ARC Facilities and hosted by David Trask, Senior Director of Customer Education & Success at ARC Facilities. The guest is Dan Keller, Assistant Vice President for Facilities & Engineering at Main Line Health Services in Philadelphia.

Keller traces his path from construction into executive healthcare facilities leadership, drawing on experience managing complex hospital systems in St. Louis and the greater Philadelphia region. The central topic is the in-house versus outsourced maintenance debate. Keller argues that investing in internal technical talent strengthens reliability, accountability and long-term operational performance, and that in-house teams help rebuild institutional knowledge that outsourcing can erode.

The conversation also covers balancing financial pressure against mission-critical healthcare operations, plus leadership practices such as psychological safety and empowering frontline teams. Keller discusses the inspiration behind his initiative The INsource Crowd and his ambition to restore pride in healthcare support services, creating cultures where people and performance improve together.

His background includes more than 20 years in healthcare facilities management, with work spanning infrastructure modernization, emergency preparedness, workforce development and operational transformation.

The post points readers to supplementary episode takeaways hosted on the ARC Facilities site, and to LinkedIn profiles for Trask and ARC Facilities. Dating in the item is inconsistent: the notice carries a September 11, 2026 dateline while referring readers to a July 21 episode.

The piece is promotional show-note content rather than reporting, with no data, survey results or vendor comparison. It sits squarely in healthcare facilities operations and maintenance strategy, and does not address workplace technology categories such as desk or room booking, visitor management, hybrid attendance policy or workplace analytics.
